metadata.title: On asymptotically optimal confidence regions and tests for high-dimensional models
metadata.authors: Sara van de Geer; Peter Bühlmann; Ya'acov Ritov; Ruben Dezeure

nodes.name: Lasso
nodes.statement: $\hat{\beta}(\lambda) := \arg\min_{\beta \in \mathbb{R}^p} \bigl( \|Y - \mathbf{X}\beta\|_2^2/n + 2\lambda \|\beta\|_1 \bigr)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Definition of the lasso estimator as the $\ell_1$-penalized least squares estimator in a $p$-dimensional linear model.

nodes.name: KKT conditions for the lasso
nodes.statement: $-\mathbf{X}^T(Y - \mathbf{X}\hat{\beta})/n + \lambda \hat{\kappa} = 0$ with $\|\hat{\kappa}\|_\infty \le 1$ and $\hat{\kappa}_j = \operatorname{sign}(\hat{\beta}_j)$ if $\hat{\beta}_j \neq 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Karush–Kuhn–Tucker first-order optimality conditions characterizing the lasso solution and its subgradient $\hat{\kappa}$.

nodes.name: Compatibility condition
nodes.statement: There exists $\phi_0 > 0$ such that for all $\beta$ with $\|\beta_{S_0^c}\|_1 \le 3 \|\beta_{S_0}\|_1$, $\|\beta_{S_0}\|_1^2 \le s_0 \beta^T \hat{\Sigma} \beta / \phi_0^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Identifiability condition on the empirical Gram matrix $\hat{\Sigma}$ relative to the active set $S_0$, with compatibility constant $\phi_0^2$.

nodes.name: Lasso for nodewise regression
nodes.statement: $\hat{\gamma}_j := \arg\min_{\gamma \in \mathbb{R}^{p-1}} \bigl( \|X_j - \mathbf{X}_{-j} \gamma\|_2^2/n + 2 \lambda_j \|\gamma\|_1 \bigr)$ for $j = 1, \ldots, p$.
nodes.statement_clean: Nodewise lasso regresses each column $X_j$ of the design on the remaining columns $\mathbf{X}_{-j}$, used to construct the relaxed inverse $\hat{\Theta}_{\mathrm{Lasso}}$.

nodes.name: Nodewise-lasso relaxed inverse $\hat{\Theta}_{\mathrm{Lasso}}$
nodes.statement: $\hat{\Theta}_{\mathrm{Lasso}} := \hat{T}^{-2} \hat{C}$, where $\hat{C}$ is built from the nodewise coefficients $\hat{\gamma}_{j,k}$ and $\hat{T}^2 = \operatorname{diag}(\hat{\tau}_1^2, \ldots, \hat{\tau}_p^2)$ with $\hat{\tau}_j^2 := \|X_j - \mathbf{X}_{-j} \hat{\gamma}_j\|_2^2/n + \lambda_j \|\hat{\gamma}_j\|_1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Approximate inverse of $\hat{\Sigma}$ assembled row by row from the nodewise lasso fits.

nodes.name: Desparsified lasso $\hat{b}_{\mathrm{Lasso}}$
nodes.statement: $\hat{b} := \hat{\beta} + \hat{\Theta} \lambda \hat{\kappa} = \hat{\beta} + \hat{\Theta} \mathbf{X}^T (Y - \mathbf{X} \hat{\beta})/n$, with $\hat{\Theta} = \hat{\Theta}_{\mathrm{Lasso}}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Bias-corrected (desparsified) version of the lasso obtained by inverting the KKT conditions with the relaxed inverse $\hat{\Theta}$.

nodes.name: Extended KKT bound $\|\hat{\Sigma} \hat{\Theta}_j^T - e_j\|_\infty$
nodes.statement: For $\hat{\Theta}_j = \hat{\Theta}_{\mathrm{Lasso},j}$ one has $\|\hat{\Sigma} \hat{\Theta}_j^T - e_j\|_\infty \le \lambda_j / \hat{\tau}_j^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Quantitative bound on how well $\hat{\Theta}_{\mathrm{Lasso}}$ inverts $\hat{\Sigma}$ row-wise; called the extended KKT condition.

nodes.name: $\ell_1$-penalized M-estimator (GLM lasso)
nodes.statement: $\hat{\beta} := \arg\min_{\beta} \bigl( P_n \rho_\beta + \lambda \|\beta\|_1 \bigr)$ for a strictly convex loss $\rho_\beta(y,x) = \rho(y, x\beta)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Generalization of the lasso to convex loss functions, yielding the $\ell_1$-penalized M-estimator used as the basis of the GLM theory.

nodes.name: Desparsified GLM estimator
nodes.statement: $\hat{b} := \hat{\beta} - \hat{\Theta} P_n \dot{\rho}_{\hat{\beta}}$, with $\hat{\Sigma} := P_n \ddot{\rho}_{\hat{\beta}}$ and $\hat{\Theta} = \hat{\Theta}_{\mathrm{Lasso}}$ from the nodewise lasso applied to $\hat{\Sigma}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Generalization of the desparsified construction to GLMs and convex losses; reduces to the linear-model formula when $\rho$ is squared error.

nodes.name: Assumption (A1) – fixed-design compatibility
nodes.statement: The compatibility condition holds for $\hat{\Sigma}$ with constant $\phi_0^2 > 0$, and $\max_j \hat{\Sigma}_{j,j} \le M^2$ for some $0 < M < \infty$.

nodes.name: Assumption (A2) – Gaussian random design
nodes.statement: Rows of $\mathbf{X}$ are i.i.d. Gaussian with inner-product matrix $\Sigma$ whose smallest eigenvalue $\Lambda_{\min}^2$ satisfies $1/\Lambda_{\min}^2 = \mathcal{O}(1)$, and $\max_j \Sigma_{j,j} = \mathcal{O}(1)$.

nodes.name: Assumptions (B1)–(B4) – (sub-)Gaussian / bounded design
nodes.statement: (B1) sub-Gaussian or (strongly) bounded i.i.d. rows; (B2) sparsity scaling $\max_j s_j \sqrt{\log(p)/n}$ or $K^2 s_j \sqrt{\log(p)/n}$ is $o(1)$; (B3) smallest eigenvalue $\Lambda_{\min}^2$ of $\Sigma$ bounded away from 0 and $\max_j \Sigma_{j,j} = \mathcal{O}(1)$; (B4) bounded fourth moment $\max_j \mathbb{E}\eta_{1,j}^4 = \mathcal{O}(K^4)$.

nodes.name: Assumptions (C1)–(C8) – GLM high-level conditions
nodes.statement: Smoothness/Lipschitz of $\dot\rho, \ddot\rho$ (C1); $\ell_1$ and prediction-norm rates for $\hat\beta$ (C2); $\|\mathbf{X}\|_\infty = \mathcal{O}(K)$ (C3); approximate inverse bound $\|P_n \ddot\rho_{\hat\beta} \hat\Theta_j^T - e_j\|_\infty = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}}(\lambda_*)$ (C4); $\|\mathbf{X}\hat\Theta_j^T\|_\infty = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}}(K)$ and $\|\hat\Theta_j\|_1 = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}}(\sqrt{s_*})$ (C5); concentration $\|(P_n - P)\dot\rho_{\beta^0}\dot\rho_{\beta^0}^T\|_\infty = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}}(K^2 \lambda)$ (C6); CLT (C7); sparsity bounds (C8).

nodes.name: Assumptions (D1)–(D5) – nodewise regression with weighted design
nodes.statement: (D1) i.i.d. data with bounded weighted design; (D2) $K^2 s_j \sqrt{\log(p)/n} = o(1)$; (D3) $\Lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_{\beta^0}) > 0$; (D4) weights $w_\beta$ bounded and locally Lipschitz; (D5) $\|\mathbf{X}(\hat\beta - \beta^0)\|_n = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}}(\lambda \sqrt{s_0})$ and $\|\hat\beta - \beta^0\|_1 = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}}(\lambda s_0)$.

nodes.name: Pivot identity for $\hat{b} - \beta^0$
nodes.statement: $\hat{\beta} - \beta^0 + \hat{\Theta} \lambda \hat{\kappa} = \hat{\Theta} \mathbf{X}^T \eps / n - \Delta/\sqrt{n}$, where $\Delta := \sqrt{n}(\hat{\Theta}\hat{\Sigma} - I)(\hat{\beta} - \beta^0)$.

nodes.name: Asymptotic pivot $\sqrt{n}(\hat{b} - \beta^0) = W + o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$
nodes.statement: $\sqrt{n}(\hat{b} - \beta^0) = W + o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$, $W \mid \mathbf{X} \sim \mathcal{N}_p(0, \sigma_\eps^2 \hat{\Theta} \hat{\Sigma} \hat{\Theta}^T)$.

nodes.name: Theorem 2.1 – fixed-design representation of $\hat{b}_{\mathrm{Lasso}}$
nodes.statement: Under (A1) and Gaussian errors, with $\lambda \ge 2 M \sigma_\eps \sqrt{2(t^2 + \log p)/n}$ and the nodewise lasso, $\sqrt{n}(\hat{b}_{\mathrm{Lasso}} - \beta^0) = W + \Delta$ with $W \sim \mathcal{N}_n(0, \sigma_\eps^2 \hat\Omega)$ and $\mathbb{P}[\|\Delta\|_\infty \ge 8\sqrt{n}(\max_j \lambda_j/\hat{\tau}_j^2)\lambda s_0/\phi_0^2] \le 2\exp[-t^2]$.
assumptions: Assumption (A1) holds with compatibility constant $\phi_0^2$ and $\max_j \hat{\Sigma}_{j,j} \le M^2$
Tuning $\lambda \ge 2 M \sigma_\eps \sqrt{2(t^2 + \log p)/n}$ and nodewise lasso (\ref{thetalasso})

nodes.name: Remark 2.1 – Studentized version of $\hat{b}_{\mathrm{Lasso}}$
nodes.statement: $\sqrt{n}(\hat{b}_{\mathrm{Lasso},j} - \beta_j^0)/(\hat\Omega_{j,j}^{1/2} \sigma_\eps) = V_j + \tilde\Delta_j$ with $V_j \sim \mathcal{N}(0,1)$ and an explicit tail bound on $\tilde\Delta_j$ depending on $\lambda_j/\tilde\tau_j$ and $\lambda/\sigma_\eps$.
nodes.statement_clean: Under the conditions of Theorem 2.1, the Studentized $\hat{b}_{\mathrm{Lasso},j}$ is asymptotically standard normal with a small remainder term.

nodes.name: Theorem 2.2 – random Gaussian design representation
nodes.statement: Under (A2), $s_0 = o(\sqrt{n}/\log p)$ and $\max_j s_j = o(n/\log p)$, with $\lambda, \lambda_j \asymp \sqrt{\log p / n}$, $\sqrt{n}(\hat{b}_{\mathrm{Lasso}} - \beta^0) = W + \Delta$, $W \mid \mathbf{X} \sim \mathcal{N}_p(0, \sigma_\eps^2 \hat\Omega)$, $\|\Delta\|_\infty = o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$, and $\|\hat\Omega - \Sigma^{-1}\|_\infty = o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$.
assumptions: Linear model (\ref{modlin}) with Gaussian errors $\eps \sim \mathcal{N}_n(0, \sigma_\eps^2 I)$, $\sigma_\eps^2 = \mathcal{O}(1)$
Sparsity $s_0 = o(\sqrt{n}/\log p)$ and $\max_j s_j = o(n/\log p)$
Tuning $\lambda \asymp \sqrt{\log p / n}$ and $\lambda_j \asymp \sqrt{\log p / n}$ uniformly in $j$

nodes.name: Corollary 2.1 – honest (uniform) confidence intervals
nodes.statement: Under (A2) and $\beta^0 \in \mathcal{B}(s_0)$ with $s_0 = o(\sqrt{n}/\log p)$, the conclusions of Theorem 2.2 hold with $\|\Delta\|_\infty = o_{\mathbb{P}_{\beta^0}}(1)$ uniformly in $\beta^0 \in \mathcal{B}(s_0)$, yielding asymptotically honest pointwise confidence intervals.

nodes.name: Theorem 2.3 – semiparametric efficiency of $\hat{b}_{\mathrm{Lasso},1}$
nodes.statement: Under condition (\ref{asyEff}) and the conditions of Theorem 2.2, $\hat{b}_{\mathrm{Lasso},1} = \beta_1^0 + n^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^n (X_{i,1} - \mathbb{E}[X_{i,1}\mid Z_i]) \eps_i + o_{\mathbb{P}}(n^{-1/2})$, attaining the semiparametric information bound $\sigma_\eps^2 / \mathbb{E}(X_{1,1} - \mathbb{E}[X_{1,1}\mid Z_1])^2$.
assumptions: Semiparametric model (\ref{asyEff}) with partially linear representation $Y = \beta_1^0 X_{,1} + K(Z) + \eps$
conclusions: Limiting variance equals the semiparametric information bound $\sigma_\eps^2 / \mathbb{E}(X_{1,1} - \mathbb{E}[X_{1,1}\mid Z_1])^2$

nodes.name: Lemma 2.1 – condition (\ref{asyEff}) holds in the canonical example
nodes.statement: In the canonical example (\ref{modsemip}) with $K(Z_1) = \sum_{j \ge 2} \beta_j^0 X_{1,j}$, fixed $s_0$, positive-definite covariance, and finite $|\{k : \gamma_{1,k} \neq 0\}|$, condition (\ref{asyEff}) is satisfied.

nodes.name: Theorem 2.4 – nodewise lasso under (sub-)Gaussian / bounded design
nodes.statement: Under (B1)–(B4) with $\lambda_j \asymp K_0 \sqrt{\log p / n}$, $\|\hat\Theta_j - \Theta_j\|_1 = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}}(K_0 s_j \sqrt{\log p / n})$, $\|\hat\Theta_j - \Theta_j\|_2 = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}}(K_0 \sqrt{s_j \log p / n})$, $|\hat\tau_j^2 - \tau_j^2| = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}}(K_0 \sqrt{s_j \log p / n})$, and the linear-model representation of Theorem 2.2 extends to non-Gaussian errors.
assumptions: Tuning $\lambda_j \asymp K_0 \sqrt{\log p / n}$ uniformly in $j$
Linear model with i.i.d. errors of variance $\sigma_\eps^2 = \mathcal{O}(1)$ (sub-exponential in the sub-Gaussian case)
conclusions: $\sqrt{n}(\hat{b}_{\mathrm{Lasso}} - \beta^0) = W + \Delta$, $W = \hat\Theta \mathbf{X}^T \eps/\sqrt{n}$, $|\Delta_j| = o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$ for every $j$ (uniform in $j$ in the sub-Gaussian / strongly bounded case)

nodes.name: Theorem 3.1 – asymptotic normality of $\hat{b}_j$ under (C1)–(C8)
nodes.statement: Under (C1)–(C8), for the desparsified GLM estimator $\hat{b}$, $\sqrt{n}(\hat{b}_j - \beta_j^0)/\hat\sigma_j = V_j + o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$ with $V_j \rightsquigarrow \mathcal{N}(0,1)$, where $\hat\sigma_j^2 := (\hat\Theta P_n \dot\rho_{\hat\beta} \dot\rho_{\hat\beta}^T \hat\Theta^T)_{j,j}$.

nodes.name: Theorem 3.2 – nodewise regression with weighted random matrices
nodes.statement: Under (D1)–(D5) with $\lambda_j \asymp K \sqrt{\log p / n}$, $\|\hat\Theta_{\hat\beta,j} - \Theta_{\beta^0,j}\|_1 = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}}(Ks_j\sqrt{\log p/n}) + \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}}(K^2 s_0((\lambda^2/\sqrt{\log p / n}) \vee \lambda))$, with analogous $\ell_2$ and $|\hat\tau^2 - \tau^2|$ rates.
conclusions: $\|\hat\Theta_{\hat\beta,j} - \Theta_{\beta^0,j}\|_1$, $\|\hat\Theta_{\hat\beta,j} - \Theta_{\beta^0,j}\|_2$, and $|\hat\tau_{\hat\beta,j}^2 - \tau_{\beta^0,j}^2|$ converge at the stated rates

nodes.name: Corollary 3.1 – simplified rates for nodewise weighted regression
nodes.statement: Under the conditions of Theorem 3.2 with $\lambda \asymp \sqrt{\log p / n}$, $K \asymp 1$, $s_j = o(\sqrt{n}/\log p)$, $s_0 = o(\sqrt{n}/\log p)$, $\|\hat\Theta_{\hat\beta,j} - \Theta_{\beta^0,j}\|_1 = o_{\mathbb{P}}(1/\sqrt{\log p})$, $\|\hat\Theta_{\hat\beta,j} - \Theta_{\beta^0,j}\|_2 = o_{\mathbb{P}}(n^{-1/4})$, and $|\hat\Theta_{\hat\beta,j}\Sigma_{\beta^0}\hat\Theta_{\hat\beta,j}^T - \Theta_{\beta^0,j,j}| = o_{\mathbb{P}}(1/\log p)$.

nodes.name: Lemma 3.1 – asymptotic-variance lemma for nodewise estimator
nodes.statement: Under the conditions of Corollary 3.1, for i.i.d. $(x_i, \xi_i)$ with $\mathbb{E} x_i^T \xi_i = 0$ and $|\xi_i| \le 1$, $\hat\Theta_{\hat\beta,j} \sum_i x_i^T \xi_i / n = \Theta_{\beta^0,j} \sum_i x_i^T \xi_i / n + o_{\mathbb{P}}(n^{-1/2})$, and $\hat\Theta_{\hat\beta,j} A \hat\Theta_{\hat\beta,j}^T \to \Theta_{\beta^0,j} A \Theta_{\beta^0,j}^T$ in probability, with the Studentized score converging weakly to $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$.

nodes.name: Theorem 3.3 – GLM asymptotic normality of $\hat{b}_j$
nodes.statement: Under conditions (i)–(vii), the desparsified GLM estimator with $\hat\Theta_{\mathrm{Lasso}}$ from (\ref{nodelassoglm}) satisfies $\sqrt{n}(\hat{b}_j - \beta_j^0)/\hat\sigma_j = V_j + o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$, $V_j \rightsquigarrow \mathcal{N}(0,1)$.
assumptions: (v) smallest eigenvalue of $\Sigma_{\beta^0}$ bounded away from zero
(vii) $s_0 = o(\sqrt{n}/\log p)$ and $s_j = \sqrt{n/\log p}$ for all $j$

nodes.name: Lemma 5.1 – $\ell_1$ bound for the lasso
nodes.statement: Under the compatibility condition with constant $\phi_0^2$ and $\hat\Sigma_{j,j} \le M^2$, with $\lambda \ge 2 M \sigma_\eps \sqrt{2(t^2+\log p)/n}$, with probability at least $1 - 2\exp(-t^2)$, $\|\hat\beta - \beta^0\|_1 \le 8 \lambda s_0/\phi_0^2$ and $\|\mathbf{X}(\hat\beta - \beta^0)\|_2^2/n \le 8\lambda^2 s_0/\phi_0^2$.
assumptions: Linear model (\ref{modlin}) with Gaussian errors and fixed design $\mathbf{X}$

nodes.name: Lemma 5.2 – random-design compatibility constant
nodes.statement: Under (A2) and $s_0 = o(n/\log p)$, with probability tending to one the empirical compatibility condition holds with $\phi_0^2 \ge 1/L^2$ for some $L = \mathcal{O}(1)$ depending on $\Lambda_{\min}$ only.
conclusions: With probability tending to one, the compatibility condition holds with $\phi_0^2 \ge 1/L^2$, $L = \mathcal{O}(1)$

nodes.name: Lemma 5.3 – uniform bound on $\max_j 1/\hat\tau_j^2$
nodes.statement: Under (A2) with $\max_j s_j = o(n/\log p)$ and tuning $\lambda_j \asymp \sqrt{\log p/n}$ uniformly in $j$, $\max_j 1/\hat\tau_j^2 = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$.

nodes.name: Lemma 5.4 – consistency $\|\hat\Omega - \Theta\|_\infty = o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$
nodes.statement: With $\hat\Theta = \hat\Theta_{\mathrm{Lasso}}$ and $\lambda_j \asymp \sqrt{\log p / n}$ uniformly in $j$, under the conditions of Lemma 5.3 and $\max_j \lambda_j^2 s_j = o(1)$, $\|\hat\Omega - \Theta\|_\infty = o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$.

nodes.name: Desparsified-Lasso (Lasso-Pro) procedure
nodes.statement: Compute the lasso $\hat\beta$, build the nodewise-lasso relaxed inverse $\hat\Theta_{\mathrm{Lasso}}$, then form the bias-corrected estimate $\hat{b}_{\mathrm{Lasso}} = \hat\beta + \hat\Theta \mathbf{X}^T(Y - \mathbf{X}\hat\beta)/n$.
input: Tuning parameters $\lambda$ for the lasso and $\{\lambda_j\}_{j=1}^p$ for the nodewise lasso
Variance estimate $\hat\sigma_\eps^2$ (e.g.\ from the scaled lasso)
output: Estimated covariance $\hat\Omega = \hat\Theta \hat\Sigma \hat\Theta^T$ for confidence intervals and tests

nodes.name: Desparsified GLM estimator (Lasso-ProG)
nodes.statement: Compute the $\ell_1$-penalized M-estimator $\hat\beta$ for a convex loss $\rho$, construct $\hat\Sigma = P_n \ddot\rho_{\hat\beta}$, run the matrix-input nodewise lasso to obtain $\hat\Theta$, and return $\hat{b} = \hat\beta - \hat\Theta P_n \dot\rho_{\hat\beta}$.
input: Tuning parameters $\{\lambda_j\}_{j=1}^p$ for the matrix-input nodewise lasso

nodes.name: Confidence regions and tests for $\beta_j^0$ in high-dimensional models
nodes.statement: Construct asymptotically valid confidence intervals and statistical tests for individual or low-dimensional components of $\beta^0$ in a high-dimensional model with $p > n$, including multiple-testing adjustment that respects dependence.

nodes.name: Riboflavin (vitamin $B_2$) production data
nodes.statement: On the Bacillus subtilis riboflavin dataset ($n=71$, $p=4088$ gene-expression covariates), the desparsified-lasso procedure finds no significant coefficient at FWER 5\% while multiple sample splitting flags one variable.

nodes.name: Simulated linear / logistic models with Toeplitz and equi-correlated designs
nodes.statement: Coverage, length, FWER and power of Lasso-Pro vs.\ residual bootstrap and multiple sample splitting on $n=100$, $p=500$ Gaussian designs with $\Sigma_{j,k} = 0.9^{|j-k|}$ (Toeplitz) and $\Sigma_{j,k} \equiv 0.8$ off-diagonal (equi-corr) for $s_0 \in \{3, 15\}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.1
nodes.statement: Bound $\|\Delta\|_\infty/\sqrt{n}$ via the extended-KKT inequality and the $\ell_1$ bound from Lemma 5.1.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.2
nodes.statement: Combine Theorem 2.1 with Lemma 5.3 to get $\|\Delta\|_\infty = o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$, and Lemma 5.4 to get $\|\hat\Omega - \Theta\|_\infty = o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.3
nodes.statement: Use uniform compatibility (Lemma 5.2) plus the population-variance bounds from (A2) and the lasso $\ell_1$-rate to control $\|X_j - \mathbf{X}_{-j}\hat\gamma_j\|_2^2/n + \lambda_j \|\hat\gamma_j\|_1$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.4
nodes.statement: Decompose $\hat\Omega = (\hat\Theta\hat\Sigma - I)\hat\Theta^T + \hat\Theta^T$ and bound each term using Lemma 5.3 and standard $\ell_2$ rates for the nodewise lasso.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.4
nodes.statement: Establish row-wise $\ell_1, \ell_2$ and $\hat\tau^2$ rates by sub-Gaussian / bounded-design concentration, then propagate to $\hat\Theta_j \Sigma \hat\Theta_j^T - \Theta_{j,j}$ and conclude as in Theorem 2.1.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.1
nodes.statement: Linearize $\dot\rho_{\hat\beta}$ around $\beta^0$ via (C1) Lipschitz of $\ddot\rho$, control remainders using (C2), (C5), (C8), and verify variance consistency using (C5)–(C6).

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.3 (GLMtheorem)
nodes.statement: Verify (C2), (C4)–(C8) for the nodewise-lasso $\hat\Theta_{\mathrm{Lasso}}$ from (\ref{nodelassoglm}) using Corollary 3.1 and Lemma 3.1, then apply Theorem 3.1.

nodes.name: Express $\|\Delta\|_\infty/\sqrt{n}$ via $(\hat\Theta\hat\Sigma - I)$
nodes.statement: $\|\Delta\|_\infty/\sqrt{n} = \|(\hat\Theta_{\mathrm{Lasso}}\hat\Sigma - I)(\hat\beta - \beta^0)\|_\infty \le \|(\hat\Theta_{\mathrm{Lasso}}\hat\Sigma - I)\|_\infty \|\hat\beta - \beta^0\|_1$.

nodes.name: Apply the extended KKT bound
nodes.statement: By the extended KKT bound (\ref{add-inver}), $\|(\hat\Theta\hat\Sigma - I)\|_\infty \le \max_j \lambda_j/\hat\tau_j^2$, so $\|\Delta\|_\infty \le \sqrt{n}\, \|\hat\beta - \beta^0\|_1 \max_j \lambda_j/\hat\tau_j^2$.

nodes.name: Plug in the $\ell_1$ bound from Lemma 5.1
nodes.statement: Substituting $\|\hat\beta - \beta^0\|_1 \le 8 \lambda s_0/\phi_0^2$ (Lemma 5.1, with probability $\ge 1 - 2\exp(-t^2)$) yields the claimed tail bound on $\|\Delta\|_\infty$.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem 2.1 with random design
nodes.statement: Theorem 2.1 plus Lemma 5.3 give $\|\Delta\|_\infty \le \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}}(s_0 \log(p)/\sqrt{n})$, which is $o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$ under $s_0 = o(\sqrt{n}/\log p)$.

nodes.name: Show $\|\hat\Omega - \Theta\|_\infty = o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$
nodes.statement: Invoke Lemma 5.4 to obtain $\|\hat\Omega - \Theta\|_\infty = o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$, completing the proof.

nodes.name: Uniform compatibility for nodewise regressions
nodes.statement: By Lemma 5.2 and a union bound, with probability tending to one the compatibility condition holds uniformly across all nodewise regressions.

nodes.name: Bound $\|X_j - \mathbf{X}_{-j}\hat\gamma_j\|_2^2/n$
nodes.statement: Standard lasso $\ell_2$-prediction rates yield $\|X_j - \mathbf{X}_{-j}\hat\gamma_j\|_2^2/n = \tau_j^2 + o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$ uniformly in $j$, with $\tau_j^2 \ge \Lambda_{\min}^2 > 0$.

nodes.name: Bound $\lambda_j \|\hat\gamma_j\|_1$
nodes.statement: Combine $\|\gamma_j\|_1 \le \sqrt{s_j \Sigma_{j,j}}/\Lambda_{\min}$ with $\|\hat\gamma_j - \gamma_j\|_1 = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}}(s_j \lambda_j)$ to obtain $\lambda_j \|\hat\gamma_j\|_1 = o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$.

nodes.name: Conclude $\max_j 1/\hat\tau_j^2 = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$
nodes.statement: Combining the previous two steps gives $\hat\tau_j^2 = \tau_j^2 + o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$ uniformly in $j$, so $\max_j 1/\hat\tau_j^2 = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$.

nodes.name: Decompose $\hat\Omega$
nodes.statement: $\hat\Omega = \hat\Theta \hat\Sigma \hat\Theta^T = (\hat\Theta\hat\Sigma - I)\hat\Theta^T + \hat\Theta^T$.

nodes.name: Bound the residual term
nodes.statement: $\|(\hat\Theta\hat\Sigma - I)\hat\Theta^T\|_\infty \le \max_j \lambda_j \|\hat\Theta_j\|_1/\hat\tau_j^2 = o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$ by Lemma 5.3 and $\|\hat\Theta_j\|_1 = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}}(\sqrt{s_j})$.

nodes.name: Bound $\|\hat\Theta - \Theta\|_\infty$
nodes.statement: $\|\hat\Theta - \Theta\|_\infty \le \max_j \|\hat\Theta_j - \Theta_j\|_2 \le \max_j \lambda_j \sqrt{s_j} = o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$.

nodes.name: Combine to conclude
nodes.statement: Combining steps 1–3 gives $\|\hat\Omega - \Theta\|_\infty = o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$.

nodes.name: Sub-Gaussian / bounded control of $\|\eta_j^T \mathbf{X}_{-j}/n\|_\infty$
nodes.statement: Concentration arguments give $\|\eta_j^T \mathbf{X}_{-j}/n\|_\infty = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}}(K_0 \sqrt{\log p / n})$, uniform in $j$ in the sub-Gaussian or strongly bounded case.

nodes.name: Establish nodewise $\ell_1, \ell_2$ rates
nodes.statement: Standard lasso analysis (with sub-Gaussian extension of restricted-eigenvalue results) yields $\|\hat\gamma_j - \gamma_j\|_1 = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}}(K_0 s_j \sqrt{\log p/n})$ and $\|\hat\gamma_j - \gamma_j\|_2 = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}}(K_0 \sqrt{s_j \log p/n})$.

nodes.name: Bound $|\hat\tau_j^2 - \tau_j^2|$
nodes.statement: Decompose $\hat\tau_j^2 - \tau_j^2$ into four terms (I–IV) and bound each using sub-Gaussian / bounded concentration, giving $|\hat\tau_j^2 - \tau_j^2| = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}}(K_0 \sqrt{s_j \log p/n})$.

nodes.name: Convert to row-wise $\hat\Theta_j$ rates
nodes.statement: Use $\hat\Theta_j = \hat C_j/\hat\tau_j^2$ and the previous bounds to obtain $\|\hat\Theta_j - \Theta_j\|_1, \|\hat\Theta_j - \Theta_j\|_2$ at the announced rates.

nodes.name: Bound the asymptotic variance gap
nodes.statement: Expand $\hat\Theta_j \Sigma \hat\Theta_j^T - \Theta_{j,j}$ using $\Theta_j \Sigma = e_j^T$ and $\hat\Theta_{j,j} = 1/\hat\tau_j^2$ to obtain the stated minimum of $\ell_1$- and $\ell_2$-type bounds.

nodes.name: Conclude representation and remainder bound
nodes.statement: $\sqrt{n}(\hat{b}_{\mathrm{Lasso},j} - \beta_j^0) = W_j + \Delta_j$ with $\Delta_j \le \sqrt{n} \lambda_j \|\hat\beta - \beta^0\|_1/\hat\tau_j^2 = o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$, uniformly in $j$ in the (sub-)Gaussian / strongly bounded case.

nodes.name: Linearize $\dot\rho_{\hat\beta}$ around $\beta^0$
nodes.statement: Write $\dot\rho(y, x_i\hat\beta) = \dot\rho(y, x_i\beta^0) + \ddot\rho(y, \tilde a_i) x_i (\hat\beta - \beta^0)$ with $\tilde a_i$ between $x_i\hat\beta$ and $x_i\beta^0$.

nodes.name: Control the remainder $\mathrm{Rem}_1$
nodes.statement: By the Lipschitz condition (C1) and (C5), $\mathrm{Rem}_1 = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}}(K \|\mathbf{X}(\hat\beta - \beta^0)\|_n^2) = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}}(K s_0 \lambda^2) = o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$ via (C2) and (C8).

nodes.name: Plug into the desparsified definition
nodes.statement: $\hat{b}_j - \beta_j^0 = -\hat\Theta_j P_n \dot\rho_{\beta^0} - \mathrm{Rem}_2$ with $|\mathrm{Rem}_2| = o_{\mathbb{P}}(n^{-1/2})$ using (C4) and the second part of (C8).

nodes.name: Verify variance consistency
nodes.statement: Bound $|(\hat\Theta P_n \dot\rho_{\hat\beta}\dot\rho_{\hat\beta}^T \hat\Theta^T)_{j,j} - (\hat\Theta P\dot\rho_{\beta^0}\dot\rho_{\beta^0}^T \hat\Theta^T)_{j,j}|$ by terms I and II of order $\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}}(K^2 s_* \lambda + K^2 \sqrt{s_0}\lambda) = o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$ using (C5)–(C6) and the last part of (C8).

nodes.name: Conclude weak convergence
nodes.statement: Combine the linearization with assumption (C7) and the variance-consistency bound to obtain $\sqrt{n}(\hat{b}_j - \beta_j^0)/\hat\sigma_j = V_j + o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)$ with $V_j \rightsquigarrow \mathcal{N}(0,1)$.

nodes.name: Verify (C2) via $\|\hat\Sigma - \Sigma_{\beta^0}\|_\infty = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}}(\lambda_*)$
nodes.statement: Compatibility for $\Sigma_{\beta^0}$ from (v) plus a locally Lipschitz argument on the empirical process yield (C2).

nodes.name: Verify (C4)–(C5) using Theorem 3.2 / Corollary 3.1
nodes.statement: Consistency of $1/\hat\tau_j^2$ for $(\Sigma_{\beta^0}^{-1})_{jj}$ (Theorem 3.2) gives (C4) at rate $\lambda_* \asymp \sqrt{\log p/n}$; row-wise $\ell_1$-control gives (C5).

nodes.name: Verify (C6) and (C7)
nodes.statement: (C6) follows from $\|\dot\rho_{\beta^0}\|_\infty = \mathcal{O}(1)$ and $\|\mathbf{X}\|_\infty = \mathcal{O}(1)$; (C7) follows from Lemma 3.1 (normallemma) since $|\Theta_{\beta^0,j} \dot\rho_{\beta^0}| = \mathcal{O}(1)$.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem 3.1
nodes.statement: With (C1)–(C8) verified, Theorem 3.1 delivers the asymptotic-normality conclusion of Theorem 3.3.

nodes.name: Compute the lasso $\hat\beta(\lambda)$
nodes.statement: Solve $\hat\beta = \arg\min_\beta \bigl(\|Y - \mathbf{X}\beta\|_2^2/n + 2\lambda \|\beta\|_1\bigr)$ for the chosen $\lambda$ (e.g.\ scaled-lasso universal value).

nodes.name: Run nodewise lasso for each $j$
nodes.statement: For $j = 1, \ldots, p$, compute $\hat\gamma_j = \arg\min_\gamma \bigl(\|X_j - \mathbf{X}_{-j}\gamma\|_2^2/n + 2\lambda_j \|\gamma\|_1\bigr)$ and $\hat\tau_j^2 = \|X_j - \mathbf{X}_{-j}\hat\gamma_j\|_2^2/n + \lambda_j \|\hat\gamma_j\|_1$.

nodes.name: Assemble $\hat\Theta_{\mathrm{Lasso}}$
nodes.statement: Form $\hat C$ from $\{\hat\gamma_{j,k}\}$, $\hat T^2 = \operatorname{diag}(\hat\tau_1^2, \ldots, \hat\tau_p^2)$ and set $\hat\Theta_{\mathrm{Lasso}} = \hat T^{-2} \hat C$.

nodes.name: Return desparsified estimate
nodes.statement: Output $\hat{b}_{\mathrm{Lasso}} = \hat\beta + \hat\Theta_{\mathrm{Lasso}} \mathbf{X}^T (Y - \mathbf{X}\hat\beta)/n$ and the variance estimate $\hat\Omega = \hat\Theta_{\mathrm{Lasso}} \hat\Sigma \hat\Theta_{\mathrm{Lasso}}^T$ for confidence intervals/tests.

nodes.name: Fit $\ell_1$-penalized M-estimator $\hat\beta$
nodes.statement: Solve $\hat\beta = \arg\min_\beta (P_n \rho_\beta + \lambda \|\beta\|_1)$ for the chosen convex loss $\rho$.

nodes.name: Form $\hat\Sigma = P_n \ddot\rho_{\hat\beta}$
nodes.statement: Compute the empirical Hessian $\hat\Sigma = P_n \ddot\rho_{\hat\beta}$ at $\hat\beta$.

nodes.name: Matrix-input nodewise lasso for $\hat\Theta$
nodes.statement: For each $j$, solve $\hat\gamma_j = \arg\min_\gamma \bigl(\hat\Sigma_{j,j} - 2\hat\Sigma_{j,\setminus j}\gamma + \gamma^T \hat\Sigma_{\setminus j,\setminus j}\gamma + 2\lambda_j \|\gamma\|_1\bigr)$ and $\hat\tau_j^2 = \hat\Sigma_{j,j} - \hat\Sigma_{j,\setminus j}\hat\gamma_j$; assemble $\hat\Theta = \hat T^{-2}\hat C$.

nodes.name: Return desparsified GLM estimate
nodes.statement: Output $\hat{b} = \hat\beta - \hat\Theta P_n \dot\rho_{\hat\beta}$ and variance $\hat\sigma_j^2 = (\hat\Theta P_n \dot\rho_{\hat\beta} \dot\rho_{\hat\beta}^T \hat\Theta^T)_{j,j}$.
